newsitem.title: UK: Singer & Friedlander still looking to expand.
newsitem.headline: Singer & Friedlander still looking to expand.

text.p: Investment bank and asset management company Singer & Friedlander Plc said on Tuesday it was still looking to expand its financial services operations.
Announcing its 1996 results, where it raised underlying pre-tax profit by 22 percent to 41.66 million stg, the bank said its expansion of financial services had proved outstandingly successful.
"We continue to search for further opportunities that meet our strict criteria," said Singer's chairman Anthony Solomons in a statement.

Singer has added broker and market maker Collins Stewart, Nordic investment banking firm Carnegie and has also expanded its retails funds and capital markets divisions in the past five years, Solomons said.
The firm has 6.0 billion stg of funds under management, an increase of 58 percent over the end of 1995.
Solomon's saw progress across the bank's activities which also include institutional and retail asset management, corporate finance and property investment.
The only negative performance came from the group's insurance broking arm Edgar Hamilton, which it has now sold, contributing an exceptional loss of 3.3 million stg.
Singer & Friedlander was mentioned as a potential bid target last year but vehemently defended its independence.

Analysts believe the company is too diverse and not a big enough player in any of its operations to present a realistic bid opportunity for a larger bank which to buy a firm as a base for a large investment banking operation based in London.
